extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and creative writers interested in folktale/narrative structure
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Vladimir Propp's morphology of the folktale: the 31 narrative 'functions' and seven character 'actant' roles used to analyze or construct Russian wonder tales (fairy tales). Useful for analyzing story events and ordering or for designing folktale-style plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative functions occur in a fixed ascending order
rubrics_metrics.description: Propp identifies 31 basic structural elements (or 'functions') that typically occur within Russian fairy tales; these functions occur in a specific, ascending order (1-31), although any given tale contains only a selection of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This syntagmatic analysis focuses on the events of a story and the order in which they occur, in contrast with paradigmatic approaches that look for underlying patterns regardless of linear order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of functions rather than all functions required
rubrics_metrics.description: After the initial situation is depicted, any wonder tale will be composed of a selection of the following 31 functions, in a fixed, consecutive order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all functions appear in every tale; the tale uses a subset but preserves relative ordering when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of inversion and repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Some functions may be inverted (for example, the hero receives an artifact of power while still at home), and typically such functions are negated twice so that they must be repeated three times in Western cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inversions change the expected placement of a function; repetition patterns (e.g., triadic repetition) are a common structural feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of the hero's community or family leaves the security of the home environment. This may be the hero himself, or some other relation that the hero must later rescue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This division of the cohesive family injects initial tension into the storyline and may serve as the hero's introduction, typically portraying him as an ordinary person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A forbidding edict or command is passed upon the hero ('don't go there', 'don't do this').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero is warned against some action; establishes a rule or constraint that shapes subsequent violation and plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of interdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior rule is violated. Therefore, the hero did not listen to the command or forbidding edict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether committed by the Hero by accident or temper, a third party or a foe, this generally leads to negative consequences. The villain enters the story via this event, though not necessarily confronting the hero directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconnaissance
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain makes an effort to attain knowledge needed to fulfil his plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disguises are often invoked as the villain actively probes for information, perhaps for a valuable item or to abduct someone; may involve speaking with a family member who innocently divulges crucial insight or seeking out the hero to gauge strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain succeeds at recon and gains a lead on his intended victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A map or information that guides subsequent villain action is often involved in this event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trickery
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain attempts to deceive the victim to acquire something valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He presses further to con the protagonists and earn their trust; sometimes the villain makes little or no deception and instead ransoms one valuable thing for another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complicity
rubrics_metrics.description: The victim is fooled or forced to concede and unwittingly or unwillingly helps the villain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The villain is now free to access somewhere previously off-limits, acting without restraint in his ploy (e.g., entry to the hero's home or a treasure vault).

rubrics_metrics.name: Villainy or lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain harms a family member (abduction, theft, spoiling crops, plundering, banishment/expulsion, murder, threatening forced marriage, nightly torments, etc.). Simultaneously or alternatively, a protagonist finds they desire or require something lacking from the home environment (potion, artifact, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The villain may be indirectly involved by fooling the family member into believing they need the missing item; establishes the problem to be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more of the negative factors comes to the attention of the Hero, who uncovers the deceit, perceives the lacking, or learns of the villainous acts that have transpired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the hero's awareness of the problem and leads to consideration of counteraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginning counteraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero considers ways to resolve the issues, by seeking a needed magical item, rescuing those who are captured, or otherwise thwarting the villain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a defining moment that shapes the hero's future actions and marks when he begins to fit his noble mantle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departure
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero leaves the home environment, this time with a sense of purpose; the adventure begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departure marks the transition from ordinary world to quest.

rubrics_metrics.name: First function of the donor
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero encounters a magical agent or helper (donor) on his path, and is tested in some manner through interrogation, combat, puzzles or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces the donor and sets up subsequent receipt of an agent contingent on hero's response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero's reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero responds to the actions of his future donor; perhaps withstanding the rigours of a test and/or failing in some manner, freeing a captive, reconciling disputing parties or otherwise performing good services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be the first time the hero comes to understand the villain's skills and powers, and uses them for good; hero's moral/behavioral qualities are revealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of a magical agent
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero acquires use of a magical agent as a consequence of his good actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be a directly acquired item, something located after navigating a tough environment, a good purchased or bartered with hard-earned resource, fashioned from parts, spontaneously summoned, a magical food consumed, or the earned loyalty/aid of another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is transferred, delivered or somehow led to a vital location, perhaps related to the donor or the location of the magical agent or its parts, or to the villain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance often moves the hero toward the next major episode or confrontation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero and villain meet and engage in conflict directly, either in battle or some nature of contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central contest or confrontation that determines victory or defeat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is marked in some manner, perhaps receiving a distinctive scar or granted a cosmetic item like a ring or scarf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Branding functions as an identifying sign used later (e.g., in recognition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Victory
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain is defeated by the hero – killed in combat, outperformed in a contest, struck when vulnerable, banished, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisive overcoming of antagonist; may precede liquidation/return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation
rubrics_metrics.description: The earlier misfortunes or issues of the story are resolved; objects of search are distributed, spells broken, captives freed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleans up the consequences of villainy and restores order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero travels back to his home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return marks the end of the journey and re-entry into the home environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is pursued by some threatening adversary, who perhaps seeks to capture or eat him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pursuit episode can generate tension after victory or during return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescue
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is saved from a chase; something may act as an obstacle to delay the pursuer, or the hero may find or be shown a way to hide, up to and including transformation unrecognisably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero's life may be saved by another; rescue resolves the pursuit episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrecognized arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero arrives, whether in a location along his journey or in his destination, and is unrecognised or unacknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets up later recognition and exposure episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfounded claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A false hero presents unfounded claims or performs some other form of deceit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be the villain, one of the villain's underlings or an unrelated party; may even be a future donor acting deceitfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficult task
rubrics_metrics.description: A trial is proposed to the hero – riddles, test of strength or endurance, acrobatics and other ordeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly used as a gate to recognition or reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero accomplishes a difficult task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates hero's worthiness and skill; often precedes recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is given due recognition – usually by means of his prior branding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal acknowledgment of the hero's identity and deeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: The false hero and/or villain is exposed to all and sundry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveals deception and clears the way for punishment and reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfiguration
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero gains a new appearance. This may reflect aging and/or the benefits of labour and health, or it may constitute a magical remembering after a limb or digit was lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves to improve his looks or signal restoration/completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain suffers the consequences of his actions, perhaps at the hands of the hero, the avenged victims, or as a direct result of his own ploy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral/justice closure for villainous acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedding
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero marries and is rewarded or promoted by the family or community, typically ascending to a throne.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventional happy ending and social restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character functions — villain
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain – an evil character that creates struggles for the hero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary source of opposition; may act directly or indirectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character functions — dispatcher
rubrics_metrics.description: The dispatcher – any character who illustrates the need for the hero's quest and sends the hero off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often overlaps with the princess's father; initiates the quest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character functions — helper
rubrics_metrics.description: The helper – a typically magical entity that comes to help the hero in their quest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides aid, objects, or advice enabling the hero to overcome obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character functions — the princess or prize (and often her father)
rubrics_metrics.description: The princess or prize, and often her father – the hero deserves her throughout the story but is unable to marry her as a consequence of some evil or injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero's journey often ends when he marries the princess, which constitutes the villain's defeat; represents the social reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character functions — donor
rubrics_metrics.description: The donor – a character that prepares the hero or gives the hero some magical object, sometimes after testing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donor tests the hero and supplies the magical agent contingent on the hero's behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character functions — hero
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero – the character who reacts to the dispatcher and donor characters, thwarts the villain, resolves any lacking or wronghoods and weds the princess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reactive figure whose moral qualities and actions drive the narrative functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character functions — false hero
rubrics_metrics.description: The false hero – a Miles Gloriosus figure who takes credit for the hero's actions or tries to marry the princess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an episode of unfounded claims and exposure leading to recognition of the true hero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and aggregation of roles
rubrics_metrics.description: These roles can sometimes be distributed among various characters, or one character can perform multiple roles (e.g., a father can send his son on the quest and give him a sword, acting as both dispatcher and donor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role distribution is flexible; analyses should allow that functions/roles may be split across or combined within characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation — Propp applied morphology specifically to wonder tales
rubrics_metrics.description: Propp applied his morphology specifically to the wonder tale (or fairy tale) in Russian folklore and based his analysis on a corpus (100 folktales from Afanasyev).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 31 functions are identified as typical of fairy/wonder tales; applying Proppian functions outside that genre requires caution.
